name: Abū Salama Ḥammād ibn Salama ibn Dīnār al-Baṣrī
summary: Basran traditionist and early grammarian, the teacher from whom Yūnus ibn Ḥabīb learned Arabic and at whose dictation Sībawayh wrote; he held that a mistake in grammar falsified a ḥadīth.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī counts Ḥammād ibn Salama among the early grammarians: Yūnus ibn Ḥabīb said he was the elder of the two and that he had learned Arabic from him. He was strict about the language of ḥadīth, saying that whoever made a grammatical mistake in his ḥadīth had lied about him.

Sībawayh wrote down ḥadīth at his dictation, and the story of his correcting the young Sībawayh's grammar is told as the reason Sībawayh turned to naḥw. Al-Zubaydī places him in the fifth generation of the grammarians of Basra.
uncertain: The year of his death: 167/784 in most sources (TDV); Ibn al-Anbārī, citing Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal through Ḥanbal ibn Isḥāq, has Dhū al-Ḥijja 169.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 50–53
Hammâd b. Seleme, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
